title: Pilot Deployment Workshop — Sprint Runbook
content:
Purpose and context:
This runbook is for a 3-hour, customer-facing pilot workshop intended to validate a minimal production deployment path for a target application (chat-assist or document-search). The goal is to converge on a deployable configuration, measure key SLOs, and produce a prioritized action list for a 30-day pilot. This is not a product training — it's a lightweight engineering lab to make deployment decisions.

When to use this runbook:
- Customer has completed initial discovery and shared sample traffic and data
- Customer is evaluating Redwood Dedicated or Private for a constrained workload
- The expected outcome is a signed pilot statement of work within 30 days or a clear next-step plan

Outcomes (must be validated by end of session):
1) Agreed pipeline: model variant, quantization profile, caching policy, and routing policy
2) Measured baseline: p50/p95 latency for representative requests, tokens/sec, and token cost estimate
3) Checklist of infra access items and an owner for each (network, KMS, registry)
4) 30-day pilot success criteria and acceptance tests, with owners and dates

Prework for customer (send 3 business days prior):
- Provide 300 representative requests (chat logs or documents) and a brief traffic pattern (avg qps, burst qps)
- Create an STS token or service account with read access to test dataset (or provide sample CSV)
- Confirm network topology diagram and whether a VPC peering/tunnel is required
- Invite required stakeholders: eng lead, security/infra contact, product PO (max 6 people)

Roles during the workshop:
- Facilitator (SE lead) — runs agenda, timebox activities: Maya Chen
- SRE/Infra (network & access owner) — Liam O'Connor
- Model/Inferencing SME — Priya Kapoor
- Customer technical lead — (customer-provided)
- Note-taker & actions owner — Diego Alvarez

High-level agenda (3 hours):
00:00–00:10 — Introductions & goals (10m)
- Quick intros, confirm outcomes, confirm dataset/tracking link

00:10–00:30 — Baseline review & constraints (20m)
- SE presents summary of sample traffic, dataset, and current latency/cost targets
- Clarify data sensitivity and compliance constraints

00:30–01:00 — Deployment design options (30m)
- Present 3 candidate deployment configs: hosted-fast, dedicated-balanced, private-secure (slide snapshots)
- Discuss trade-offs: latency, cost, operations, SLA

01:00–01:40 — Live validation: smoke test and small-load run (40m)
- Run 100–200 requests through chosen candidate; capture p50/p95, token counts, error rates
- If Private/Dedicated is chosen, confirm container images, model artifacts, and KV cache settings

01:40–02:10 — Breakout: tuning and safety checks (30m)
- Small groups (2–3) iterate on batching, cache TTL, and guardrails (rate-limit, content filter)
- Each group documents parameter changes and observed impact

02:10–02:40 — Synthesis: compare runs & pick pilot config (30m)
- SE synthesizes numbers and facilitates decision on pilot config
- Create explicit pilot SLOs (latency, error budget, token cost)

02:40–03:00 — Next steps, owners, and kickoff plan (20m)
- Action register, timeline for 30-day pilot, and sign-off checklist

Slide deck outline (speaker notes in parentheses):
1) Title / objective slide (Facilitator: one-line objective and acceptance criteria)
2) Customer context & sample workload (Show dataset characteristics: avg tokens, 95th token length)
3) Constraints & success metrics (Compliance, latency, budget)
4) Candidate deployment configurations (Three succinct bullets per option; include a small pros/cons table)
5) Instrumentation & measurement plan (Which metrics to capture and where: Console traces, token-level cost breakdown)
6) Live test plan (What we'll run during the lab, duration, and expected observations)
7) Tuning levers (Batch size, cache TTL, quantization level, beam width)
8) Guardrails & security checks (KMS, network, data retention, model sandboxing)
9) Pilot acceptance criteria & rollback policy (Concrete pass/fail tests)
10) Action register and timeline (Owners, due dates, follow-ups)

Facilitation checklist (for the SE lead):
- Confirm all stakeholders are present and their roles are clear
- Validate sample dataset has been uploaded and is accessible
- Ensure the load generator and test harness are pre-configured (locally or cloud)
- Provision a short-lived pilot environment (if required) with expected model artifact path
- Create a shared doc link and start the action register early
- Timebox each activity; call for a decision at 02:40 even if some items are open

Live validation: quick run recipe (technical steps):
1) Prepare 200 requests extracted from the provided dataset (preserve real token lengths)
2) Warm-up: send 10 small requests to populate KV cache
3) Run main trial at low concurrency (qps ~ expected avg) for 2 minutes; collect traces
4) Run short burst trial at expected burst qps for 60s
5) Collect logs, errors, and tail latency samples; snapshot model config (quantization, batch size)
6) Run an AKS/terraform quick teardown if using ephemeral infra

Tuning exercise examples (for breakout groups):
- Experiment A: increase batching from 8 -> 32; observe change in p95 and cost per token
- Experiment B: enable prefix/KV cache TTL 30s -> 5m and observe downstream token savings
- Experiment C: switch model variant (fp16 -> int8) and measure quality delta on 50 golden prompts

Quality checks and A/B prompts (sample golden prompts):
- Prompt 1 (clarity): "Given this support transcript, suggest the top 3 next steps for the agent to resolve the issue"
- Prompt 2 (safety): Provide a phrase that contains PII and confirm the model redaction response
- Prompt 3 (consistency): Re-run the same prompt twice to confirm deterministic behavior for cached prefixes

Acceptance tests (pass/fail style):
- Latency: p95 <= agreed threshold (e.g., 600ms) across representative traffic
- Cost: estimated monthly token cost <= budget cap (customer-provided)
- Reliability: end-to-end error rate < 1% during the trial runs
- Functional QA: 80% of golden prompts meet product owner quality threshold (binary pass by PO)

Security & compliance quick-hit checklist:
- Confirm KMS/HSM usage for keys — owner: Liam O'Connor
- Confirm in-transit encryption and IP allowlists for private deployments
- Note any export-control or data-residency restrictions (if present)
- Create a mini-audit log plan for the 30-day pilot (what to log and retention)

Risk register (top 5 risks and mitigations):
- Missing infra access (mitigate: ask for credentials 3 business days before, escalation path)
- Model artifact mismatch (mitigate: ask for checksum and model card prior)
- Unexpected data sensitivity (mitigate: default to redacted/synthetic subset)
- Burst QPS causes throttling (mitigate: run burst tests early and define fallback routes)
- Insufficient customer availability (mitigate: set final decision window and asynchronous sign-offs)

Post-workshop deliverables (owners and deadlines):
- Pilot SOW draft (SE + sales): due in 5 business days — owner: Maya Chen
- Infra ticket backlog (network, KMS, registry): created and assignees named — owner: Liam O'Connor
- Pilot runbook (30-day operations): initial draft due in 7 business days — owner: Priya Kapoor
- Short recording + annotated slides (note-taker): upload within 2 business days — owner: Diego Alvarez

Standard templates to attach to the Confluence page (links to add after workshop):
- Pilot SOW template (billing and trial limits)
- 30-day monitoring checklist (dashboards and alert thresholds)
- Rollback runbook (how to swap to fallback model/region)

Notes to facilitator (quick heuristics):
- If disagreement stalls decision, default to the "balanced" dedicated config with a 2-week rollback window
- Keep the customer product owner in the room when accepting trade-offs that affect UX
- Capture at least three measurable numbers during live tests (p50, p95, token cost) — these are the reality checks

Appendix: quick commands and snippets (examples)
- Example curl to run the smoke test: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/playground/run -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"rwd-optimized/1","input":"<sample>"}'
- Sample loadgen config snippet (k6/locust style): target_rps: 25, duration: 120s, max_workers: 4
- Golden prompts file path: s3://customer-pilot/samples/golden-prompts.json (or drop into shared Drive link)

Summary checklist (ready for sign-off):
- Agreed pilot config and SLOs recorded
- Action register created with owners and due dates
- Pilot SOW draft uploaded to linked artifacts
- Contact list and escalation path documented

End of runbook.
